supersedes_design_draft.reason: Clarify the exact design-level candidate-panel FPR estimand and prohibit empirical or policy-weighted same-FPR interpretations.

purpose: Test whether switching which frozen wrong identity receives the second positive reward changes where one-step transfer appears, while BUG_ALIGNED and BUG_PERMUTED have the same frozen candidate panel, the same unweighted design-level candidate-panel FPR, and the same unweighted binary reward-vector mass.

provenance_and_outcome_awareness.relationship_to_r11: NEW DRAFT ONLY. This file does not amend, supersede, authorize, or modify the frozen R11 package.
provenance_and_outcome_awareness.outcome_awareness: R12 was designed after R10 development outcomes and after an identification audit of R11. It can never be relabelled confirmatory.
provenance_and_outcome_awareness.design_freeze_rule: Any change to arms, FPR definitions, derangement, stacks, estimands, gates, or evidence boundaries requires a new schema version and independent review before authorization.

why_r11_is_not_shared_identity_causal_pr: R11 intervenes on BUG versus GOLD_ONLY and can identify the effect of adding a frozen false-positive reward relative to clean gold-only learning under its fixed one-step setup.
R11 does not intervene on whether the rewarded wrong identity is aligned or misaligned with the target identity.
R11 structural excess D contrasts target columns of the same observed matrix; it is fixed-codebook treatment-effect heterogeneity, not a randomized identity-alignment intervention.
R11's 120 identity-bijection enumeration re-labels the same observed outcomes and is a deterministic sensitivity diagnostic, not an inferential randomization test.
Therefore an R11 pass cannot by itself establish that shared result identity is the causal channel.

fixed_candidate_panel_and_fpr_definition.design_candidate_panel_fpr_definition: number of negative candidates assigned positive binary reward divided by the six frozen negative candidates in that row

matched_reward_vector_mass.definition: unweighted sum of the seven binary reward entries per row

fixed_candidate_panel_and_fpr_definition.not_empirical_fpr: The fixed 1/6 quantity is a design-level, unweighted candidate-panel ratio. It is not calibrated from observed verifier errors over a task population or natural model outputs.
fixed_candidate_panel_and_fpr_definition.not_policy_weighted_fpr: The experiment does not match or estimate a policy-weighted FPR. Candidate probabilities can differ, so the rewarded wrong candidate can carry different policy probability mass in the two BUG arms even though both have design FPR 1/6.
fixed_candidate_panel_and_fpr_definition.not_equal_expected_reward: Equal binary reward-vector mass does not imply equal pre-update expected reward under the model policy; that difference is neither matched nor called FPR.

canonical_pilot_stacks.selection_rule: Use the first M0/A_TO_B stack in the pre-existing frozen order for each task pair; do not select by outcomes.
canonical_pilot_stacks.statistical_boundary: The two task pairs are development cases only. Stacks, identities, target cells, processes, and technical replicates are not additional independent task-pair samples.

GOLD_ONLY.reward_mask_rule: gold=1; all six frozen negative candidates=0
GOLD_ONLY.role: clean-learning anchor for A; not part of the same-design-FPR identity-switch contrast

BUG_ALIGNED.reward_mask_rule: gold=1; frozen wrong candidate for source identity r=1; all other candidates=0

BUG_PERMUTED.reward_mask_rule: gold=1; frozen wrong candidate for identity pi(r) under CYCLIC_PLUS_ONE_R1=1; all other candidates=0

held_equal: one gold and six negative candidates per row
two positive binary reward entries and reward-vector mass of 2
tokenizer, chat template, batching, optimizer, learning rate, clipping threshold, precision, model, and dependency inventory
identity_switch_control.only_permitted_difference: which frozen wrong identity receives the second positive binary reward: r versus pi(r)
unmatched_and_reported: pre-update policy probability assigned to the selected wrong candidate
identity_switch_control.gold_contrast_boundary: GOLD_ONLY differs from both BUG arms in design FPR and binary reward-vector mass. A is a clean-anchor error-addition contrast, not a same-design-FPR contrast.

MINIMAL_6_PROCESS.process_formula: 2 stacks x 3 arms x 1 technical replicate
MINIMAL_6_PROCESS.count_check: 6 processes x 5 source identities x 5 target identities = 150 target cells

REPRODUCIBILITY_12_PROCESS.process_formula: 2 stacks x 3 arms x 2 technical replicates
REPRODUCIBILITY_12_PROCESS.count_check: 12 processes x 5 source identities x 5 target identities = 300 target cells; A/B are technical repeats, not independent scientific samples

execution_variants.preauthorization_choice_rule: Select and freeze exactly one variant before authorization. Running A under the 6-process variant, inspecting outcomes, and conditionally adding B is forbidden.

potential_outcomes_and_estimands.outcome: Y(k,s,r,q,arm) is the frozen post-update target metric for replicate k, stack s, source identity r, target identity q, and arm; pre traces must be identical across arms.
potential_outcomes_and_estimands.C_sign_check: If alignment causally redirects transfer toward the rewarded wrong identity, Y_ALIGNED-Y_PERMUTED should be larger at q=r than at q=pi(r), so the pre-specified supporting direction is C>0.
potential_outcomes_and_estimands.A_boundary: A>0 supports an aligned false-positive addition effect relative to GOLD_ONLY in this panel, but A is not a same-design-FPR estimand.
potential_outcomes_and_estimands.C_boundary: C is the primary same-design-FPR, equal-binary-reward-mass identity-switch estimand. It does not establish matched policy-weighted FPR.
aggregation_order: compute A and C within replicate k and exact (s,r)
under the 12-process variant, require replicate matrices to agree within 1e-12 before equal averaging
equal-average five fixed source identities within each selected task-pair stack
report the two task-pair means separately before any descriptive overall average
report every identity-level value without treating nested values as independent samples
potential_outcomes_and_estimands.inference_boundary: With two task-pair clusters, no standard error, confidence interval, inferential p-value, or population-level task claim is permitted.

technical_pass_requires_all: complete the selected 6-process or 12-process design with no missing, duplicate, swapped, or extra cell
recompute exact canonical reward masks and verify GOLD_ONLY=0/6, BUG_ALIGNED=1/6, and BUG_PERMUTED=1/6 design FPR on every row
verify binary reward-vector masses of 1, 2, and 2 for GOLD_ONLY, BUG_ALIGNED, and BUG_PERMUTED respectively
verify BUG_ALIGNED and BUG_PERMUTED differ only in r versus pi(r) for the second rewarded candidate
match all non-treatment source, target, candidate, model, checkpoint, initial-state, update, evaluator, and environment bindings
fresh checkpoint reset before every source identity
no realized gradient clipping and all values finite
under the 12-process variant, all A/B adjusted target matrices agree within absolute tolerance 1e-12
development_decision_rule.gate_consistency_note: The overall sign gates are redundant once both equally weighted task-pair means are positive; they are retained only as explicit summary integrity checks and do not create additional evidence.

failure_labels.A_GATE_FAILURE: No consistent aligned false-positive addition effect relative to GOLD_ONLY; stop this bridge mechanism.
failure_labels.C_GATE_FAILURE_WITH_A_POSITIVE: A false-positive effect may exist, but the rewarded wrong identity has not been shown to causally redirect transfer; prohibit the shared-identity claim.
failure_labels.TECHNICAL_GATE_FAILURE: No scientific interpretation. Repair under a new frozen version; outcome-dependent retry is forbidden.

development_decision_rule.identity_heterogeneity_policy: Report all five fixed identity-level A and C values. Identity unanimity is not a minimum-pilot gate, and identities are not independent samples; any negative identity remains an explicit boundary condition.
development_decision_rule.stop_after_result: Any failure ends this draft version. No adaptive arm, FPR definition, stack, identity, threshold, derangement, or hyperparameter change is permitted within the same version.

result_validator_minimum_requirements: recompute canonical reward masks from bound rows, ordered candidates, arm, r, and pi(r); a merely non-empty mask string is insufficient
recompute design-level candidate-panel FPR and binary reward-vector mass row by row
record but do not relabel policy probability mass or expected reward as FPR
bind each result to its arm contract, execution manifest, authorization receipt, and invocation receipt
reject arm swaps, derangement drift, mask tampering, cross-arm drift, cross-replicate binding drift, clipping, and missing cells
recompute A, DeltaSwitch, and C from raw target metrics
label all summaries development-only and non-inferential

claim_boundary.can_support_if_passed: Development-only evidence, within the same frozen seven-candidate panel and two selected affine-codebook task pairs, that switching the rewarded wrong identity from r to pi(r) changes relative one-step target transfer while BUG_ALIGNED and BUG_PERMUTED have the same unweighted design candidate-panel FPR of 1/6 and the same binary reward-vector mass of 2.
cannot_support: independence of processes, technical replicates, identities, or target cells
claim_boundary.next_stage_if_passed: Freeze a separate design with at least six new outcome-independent task-pair clusters, an externally justified magnitude margin, and an explicit empirical or policy-weighted FPR calibration if any broader same-FPR claim is desired.
